claim: arch_mapping_store.md states the lookup contract twice — "Provide lookup by identity hash or by task id — the two keys are interchangeable ways to reach one node" (Responsibilities) and "resolve one key, hash or task id, to its fold entry — including removed nodes, whose entries carry the biography instead of a live task" (Interface) — while test_mapping_store.md's "Removed node retains its biography" scenario expects only that "a lookup still returns its name, node_type, module and the removing event's proposal and git_head", naming no key.
authoritative_source: flow_bead_mapping.md (~line 124): a cleanup bead is not a dangling reference because "its task id resolves through the journal to the removed node's biography" — the task-id direction is required for removed nodes, and arch_context_resolver.md depends on it ("its journal pairing references the removal event, so the task id resolves to enough context to run `git show` on the retired leaf").
evidence: Three holes, all in the same contract. (1) The test leaf's unnamed key: a hash-only implementation satisfies test_mapping_store.md while violating arch_mapping_store.md's interchangeable-keys clause, and that is exactly what shipped — `spex map context spexmachina-f6eh.1` returned "not found: task" for a node `spex map context 06035e7f0c39` resolved, with CI green throughout. No scenario pins the removed-node-by-task-id direction. (2) Nothing states that receipt-to-event pairing is by eid regardless of file position. "In file order" appears only for parse and for list ordering; the dangling edge case says "names an eid no change event carries", which supports position-independence but does not state it. The real journal appends a cleanup's task_created ahead of the removal event it names (line 684 vs 782 of spec/.history.jsonl), and both fold and History read the pairing positionally, dropping 15 cleanup pairings across the f6eh cohort. (3) Whether a removed node keeps its PRE-removal task id is undecided. "Instead of a live task" admits both readings; the fix takes the narrow one (the removal supersedes the pre-removal pairing, the cleanup task id survives) because ingest/reconciler.go buildCleanupCreate uses `Removed && TaskID != ""` as its "cleanup already landed" idempotency signal and would skip real cleanup receipts under the broad reading. That dependency is stated in no spec leaf, so a future implementer reading only the spec could broaden it and silently break cleanup idempotency.
proposed_fix: In test_mapping_store.md, name the key in the removed-node scenario and add a scenario keying a removed node by its cleanup task id, plus one where the receipt precedes the removal event in the file. In arch_mapping_store.md, state that receipts pair to change events by eid and never by file position, and state explicitly which task id a removed entry carries (the cleanup task, not the superseded pre-removal one) so the ingest-side idempotency signal rests on a written contract.
